title: Glass Bottle
sub: Four tools: Line, Revolve, Shell, Fillet
say: In this tutorial we'll model a glass bottle in OpenShape 3D, using just four tools: Line, Revolve, Shell and Fillet. Everything you'll see is done through the touch interface, so you can follow along on your own iPad.

title: A blank design
lines: Undo, views, Items and History on top
say: Start a blank design. The tool palette sits on the left. The toolbar on top has undo and redo, the standard views, and the Items and History panels.

title: Step 1 · Pick a plane
sub: Sketch › Line, then the front plane
lines: A bottle is a revolved shape
Draw half the profile, standing up
say: Tap Sketch, then Line. The app asks which plane to sketch on. A bottle is a revolved shape, so we'll draw half of its profile standing up, on the front plane. Tap the blue tile.

title: Step 2 · Centerline
sub: Two taps, then an exact height
lines: Tap the base, tap the top
say: Start with the centerline. Tap once at the base and once at the top, then tap Line again to finish. The line stays selected, so tap its dimension badge and type the height: two hundred and thirty millimeters. Fit View brings it back on screen.

title: Step 3 · Draw the outline
lines: Start at the top of the centerline
Out to the lip, down the neck
Over the shoulder, down the body
Finish at the base: the profile closes
say: Now the outline. Pick Line again and start at the top of the centerline. Each tap adds a corner and the line carries on from the last one: out to the lip, down the neck, over the shoulder, down the body, and in at the base. Finish on the bottom of the centerline, and the profile closes and fills in.

title: Step 4 · Revolve
sub: Tap the fill, choose Revolve, tap the axis
say: Exit the sketch and tap inside the filled profile. The bar offers Extrude by default. Choose Revolve instead, then tap the centerline to use it as the axis. A full three hundred and sixty degrees, and the flat profile becomes a solid bottle.

title: Step 5 · Material
sub: Select the body, Material, pick a preset
lines: Looks only: the geometry stays exact
say: Let's color it now so the next steps are easier to see. Double-tap the bottle to select it, open Material, and pick a preset or a custom color. Apply. This only changes the look. The geometry underneath stays exact.

title: Step 6 · Shell
sub: Modify › Shell, open the mouth, 2 mm
lines: Tap the top face to leave it open
say: Now make it hollow. Tap Modify, then Shell. Tap the top face so the mouth stays open, type a wall thickness of two millimeters, and Apply. The solid becomes a thin glass wall.

title: Step 7 · Fillet
sub: Modify › Fillet, tap the rim, 1 mm
lines: One tap picks the whole rim
say: Finally, round the lip. Tap Modify, then Fillet, and tap the rim. One tap picks the whole circular edge. Type a one millimeter radius and Apply.

title: Every step stays editable
lines: Change the thickness or the profile
Export STEP, STL, 3MF, OBJ or DXF
say: Open History and every step is still there: change the wall thickness or move a corner of the profile, and the bottle rebuilds. When you're happy, export STEP or STL from the share menu.

title: That's a bottle
say: That's a glass bottle in four tools. OpenShape 3D is free and open source, with no account and no cloud. Thanks for watching, and happy modeling.
